It disgusts me to watch this.

He smells of a floral scent.

The bullet struck him dead.

I'm learning Korean.

The city celebrated its thousandth anniversary.

The engine won't start, check the ignition.

Crucian carp breed in the pond.

note: разводи́ться с + instr.: to divorce someone

Expenses exceed income.
He believes in miraculous healing.
The healing came unexpectedly.

note: bookish; in speech: выздоровле́ние (recovery)

examples.en: His finger rested on the trigger.
The trigger mechanism went off.

note: «спусково́й крючо́к» = trigger

examples.en: A bunny is hopping across the grass.
A spot of sunlight is dancing on the wall.

note: also a reflected light spot: со́лнечный за́йчик

examples.en: I'm having money trouble.
He found himself in a bind.

note: «быть в затрудне́нии» = to be at a loss

examples.en: The doctor examined the patient.
The building needs to be inspected.

note: a medical or professional examination

examples.en: He didn't live to see retirement.
I want to live to be a hundred.

note: дожи́ть до + gen.; to live through = пережи́ть

He dug an old coin out of the ground.

Well done, my clever girl!

note: colloquial, affectionate; praise for a child

note: «доводи́ть до слёз» = to reduce to tears

The harvest is dying because of drought.

note: past tense: гиб, ги́бла (without -ну-)

The old man keeps a little shop.

note: a flatterer; in church use: a saint (уго́дник Бо́жий)

The inhaler is in the bag.
Speak of the devil!
There has been no sign of him for a long time.

note: only in set phrases: лёгок на по́мине

examples.en: I'll be happy for you.
The children were delighted with the presents.

note: порадоваться + dat.: to be glad about; за + acc.: for someone

examples.en: The pilot lowered the landing gear.
The truck's chassis broke.

note: indeclinable; both a vehicle chassis and an aircraft's landing gear

examples.en: We decorated the New Year tree.
Spruces grow in the forest.

note: the New Year tree; the tree itself is ель (spruce)

He likes London fog.

The airline canceled the flight.

It's hard to make out faces in the dark.

This is Saudi oil.

She kept silent on purpose.
Let me finish.
He didn't get to finish and fell silent.

related.en: to agree, to come to an agreement

note: «договори́ться» means to come to an agreement; договори́ть means to finish speaking.

examples.en: The doctor is examining the patient.
We spent the whole day looking around the city.
We managed to sneak food into the concert.

examples.ru: Она [пронесла́] эту любовь через всю жизнь.
examples.en: She carried this love with her all her life.

related.en: to carry through, to carry past

note: «пронести́сь» means to rush past: ветер пронёсся.

examples.en: A mouse is squeaking in the corner.
The phone is beeping: the battery is running low.
Santa Claus (Ded Moroz) rides in a sleigh.
Old sleds are standing in the storage room.

note: Plural only; a child's sled is са́нки.

examples.en: We need to assess the situation soberly.
He takes a sober view of life.
I had to sweat over this problem.
We had a good sweat in the sauna.

note: colloq.: попоте́ть над чем-то = to work hard on something.

examples.en: This fearless man saved three children.
She is a fearless journalist.

examples.en: He gave in to temptation.
The door finally gave way.

note: + dat.: подда́ться иску́шению (give in to temptation), подда́ться угово́рам (yield to persuasion).

examples.en: This painting is the crowning achievement of his work.
The bride put the wreath on her head.

note: под вене́ц = to the altar, into marriage.

examples.en: What a sweet baby!

note: Feminine in form, but can refer to a boy: он такой малю́тка.

Diamond consists of carbon.
Carbon emissions are rising.

note: Not to be confused with у́голь (coal).

examples.en: The boat pulled up to the shore.
He pestered me with questions.

note: приста́ть к кому-то (colloq.) = to pester someone.

examples.en: He lives off his investments.
They get rental income from renting out their apartment.

related.en: rentier, person living on investment income

The police questioned the witnesses.

note: расспроси́ть о ком-то / о чём-то (о + prep.).

note: Bookish.

related.en: on one's knees, on one's lap

The light turned green at the traffic light.

note: загоре́ться иде́ей = to get fired up about an idea.

I had a weird dream.

He found himself in the very hell of the battle.

note: Colloq.; often means sweltering heat, not just hell.

The animals' habitat has changed.

note: Bookish.

Diabetics need insulin.
The pancreas produces insulin.

note: Stress on the last syllable: инсули́н.

note: Impersonal, + dat.: мне живётся хорошо = life is good for me.

examples.en: What an amazing view!
This is wonderful music.

Cut out a narrow strip of paper.

Hand in your documents at window number three.

note: Diminutive of окно́; also a service window, a counter.

He became an accomplice to the crime.
He feels drawn to adventure.

She has thin hair.

note: жи́дкие во́лосы = thin hair.

letter (of the alphabet) — a written sign: большая бу́ква, a capital letter

matter, business, case — abstract: не твоё де́ло, none of your business

lazy — an adjective: лени́вый челове́к, a lazy person

light — включи́ свет, turn on the light

to pee — child talk and colloquial

now (as opposed to before) — a change from an earlier state

light blue, sky blue — голубо́е не́бо, a light blue sky

chair — сесть на стул, to sit down on a chair
capital city — столи́ца страны́, the capital of a country

examples.en: Russia is a big country.

Open the book to page five.

side, direction — пра́вая сторона́, the right side
page (of a book) — страни́ца кни́ги, a page of a book

examples.en: Keep the receipt in case you want to return the item.

bill, check — in a restaurant; account — счёт в ба́нке, a bank account

examples.en: An avocado costs one hundred rubles apiece.

pike — a fish: лови́ть щу́ку, to catch a pike

examples.en: Raspberry is a tasty berry.

We picked wild strawberries in the forest.

wild strawberry — the small forest one

examples.en: She has a red dress.
What a beautiful city!

examples.en: The film lasts two hours.
Old clocks hang on the wall.
We have six lessons tomorrow.

related.en: clock, watch — used only in the plural

examples.en: The bread is from yesterday, already stale.

Have some strong tea.

related.en: hard, firm, solid — of ice, ground, a surface
strong, sturdy — of tea, sleep, health, a rope

examples.en: We have lunch at two o'clock.
At afternoon snack time the kids eat cookies.
There will be fish for dinner today.

related.en: afternoon snack — between lunch and dinner

note: Breakfast is «за́втрак».

examples.en: A black storm cloud hangs over the city.
There is not a single cloud in the sky.

related.en: storm cloud — a dark cloud full of rain or thunder

examples.en: I don't regret my decision.
He is always complaining about life.

related.en: to regret, to feel sorry for; to spare — «не жале́ть сил»

note: «Жале́ть» also means «to spare»: «не жале́ть сил» (to spare no effort).

examples.en: Give me a pen, I'll write it down.

related.en: pen — a writing pen with ink; also a handle

examples.en: I was born in a big city.

related.en: hail — ice falling from the clouds

note: The old word «град» (city) survives mostly in names: Белгра́д, Волгогра́д.

examples.en: I stopped by the store to get some bread.

related.en: magazine — a periodical, also a journal

examples.ru: Его положили в [пала́ту] на втором этаже.
examples.en: He was put in a ward on the second floor.

The children are playing in the yard.

related.en: palace — a grand building of a ruler
yard, courtyard; also a royal court

examples.en: His cup of patience has overflowed.

Drink a cup of tea while it's hot.

related.en: goblet, bowl — festive or figurative: «чаша терпения»
glass, tumbler — for water and juice, no handle

note: A shot glass is «рю́мка».

examples.en: Tell me the whole truth.
I believe in justice.

note: In conversation «Пра́вда?» also means «Really?».

examples.en: On Saturdays we go to the bathhouse.

related.en: bathhouse, Russian sauna — steamy, usually wooden
resort, spa — a place for vacation or treatment
bathroom — the room with the bath in an apartment

examples.en: A red squirrel lives in the park.

examples.en: Our driver is very careful.

related.en: host, presenter — of a TV or radio show

examples.en: A coat of arms is shown on the coin.

note: A hunchbacked person is «горба́тый».

examples.en: The witch was brewing a potion in a cauldron.
Add some fresh greens to the salad.

related.en: fresh herbs, greens — parsley, dill and the like

examples.en: She took a cookie with her coffee.

related.en: roast — meat with vegetables cooked in an oven or pan

examples.en: We keep potatoes in the cellar.

related.en: cellar — an underground room for storing food
basement — the lower floor of a building

examples.en: The bank lowered the interest rate.
He placed a bet on his favorite team.
A new expense item has appeared in the budget.

related.en: article (in a paper); item (in a budget)

examples.en: A flock of ducks is flying over the lake.
The cow is standing in the cowshed.
The horse went back to the stable.

related.en: flock, pack — of birds, wolves, dogs: «во́лчья ста́я»
cowshed, pigsty — for cattle and pigs

examples.en: Don't touch the wire, it's live!
The current carried the boat away.

examples.ru: В [тече́ние] недели я буду в отъезде.
examples.en: I'll be away this week.

related.en: current, flow of water; «в тече́ние» means «during, over the course of»

examples.ru: У нас с тобой есть общее [де́ло].
examples.en: You and I have a cause in common.
This work was written in the nineteenth century.

related.en: a work — of literature, art or music

note: «Как дела́?» means «How are things?».

examples.en: Don't ask me about that.
He is trying to open the window.
I eat at home.

related.en: to eat, to feed oneself — «питаться до́ма»

note: «Пыта́ть» without «-ся» means «to torture».

examples.en: My favorite color is blue.
She gave me a flower.

note: The plural «цветы́» means flowers, «цвета́» means colors.

examples.en: Documents must be kept in a safe.

examples.ru: Мама [ко́рмит] кота два раза в день.
examples.en: Mom feeds the cat twice a day.

related.en: to keep, to store — in a safe place
to feed — a child, an animal

examples.en: Flour is needed for blini.
Waiting is agony.

note: Two different words spelled the same, told apart only by stress: «мука́» (flour) and «му́ка» (torment, pl. «му́ки»).

examples.en: The fridge is completely empty.
Don't ask idle questions.

note: «Пра́здный» is bookish: «пра́здное любопы́тство» (idle curiosity).

examples.en: A rainbow appeared after the rain.
An electric arc dazzles the eyes.

related.en: arc, curve — an electric arc, the bow of a horse's harness

examples.en: He never forgave her betrayal.
The schedule has changed.

note: The verb «измени́ть» means both «to change» (+ acc.) and «to betray, be unfaithful to» (+ dat.).

examples.en: He is too stingy to leave a tip.
This coat is too expensive.

note: «Дорого́й» also means «dear»: «дорого́й друг».

examples.en: The money goes into the treasury.
They abolished the death penalty in that country.
What punishment did he get?

note: A fine is «штраф»; the death penalty is «сме́ртная казнь».

examples.en: I have a headache.
I read the first chapter of the book.

note: «Глава́ семьи́» means «head of the family».

examples.ru: Ночью стало холодно, и я взял второе [одея́ло].
examples.en: It got cold at night, so I took a second blanket.
I wear these clothes at home.

related.en: clothes, clothing — a collective noun, no plural

examples.en: He likes catching fish.
In his youth my grandfather hunted wild boar.

note: «Лови́ть» means to catch: «лови́ть ры́бу», «лови́ть мяч». A hunter is «охо́тник».

examples.en: I'm learning the words for the exam.
My sister studies at the university.
He is studying art history.
In the evenings I study English.

related.en: to learn something; to teach someone — «учи́ть слова́», «учи́ть ребёнка»
to study, to be a student — «он у́чится в шко́ле»
to work on something, to do — «занима́ться спо́ртом»

note: «Учи́ть» takes an object: «учи́ть слова́», «учи́ть ребёнка». Without an object, or with an infinitive, use «учи́ться»: «он у́чится в шко́ле», «она́ у́чится води́ть» (she is learning to drive).

examples.en: Do you know his phone number?
My daughter can read.
I can't come tomorrow.

related.en: to know — a fact, a person, an answer: «зна́ть отве́т»
to know how to, can — a learned skill
can, to be able to — possibility or permission

note: For a learned skill use «уме́ть»: «я уме́ю пла́вать» (I can swim), not «я зна́ю пла́вать». «Зна́ть» is not used with an infinitive.

examples.en: I always put my keys in my pocket.
Put the book on the table.
You are putting the bottle on the shelf.
We are hanging the picture on the wall.

related.en: to put, to lay — so that it lies flat: «кла́сть кни́гу на стол»
to put, to lay (pf. of «кла́сть») — «положи́ть телефо́н на стол»
to put, to stand — upright: «ста́вить ча́шку, буты́лку»

note: Where English says «put», Russian picks a verb by the position of the object: lying (кла́сть), standing (ста́вить) or hanging (ве́шать).

examples.en: I like listening to music.
Do you hear that noise?

note: «Слу́шать» is on purpose, «слы́шать» is by chance: «Я слы́шал, что...» (I heard that...), «слу́шай меня́» (listen to me).

examples.en: In the evening we watch a movie.
I can't see without glasses.

note: «Смотри́ на меня́» means «look at me», «я тебя́ ви́жу» means «I see you».

examples.en: He speaks English well.
He said he would come.
We talked on the phone for a long time.

related.en: to speak, to talk — a language or an ongoing action: «говори́ть по-ру́сски»
to say, to tell (pf.) — one statement
to talk, to have a conversation — «разгова́ривать по телефо́ну»

note: A language is always «spoken» with «говори́ть»: «говори́ть по-ру́сски». «Сказа́ть» is perfective: «он сказа́л, что...» (he said that...).

examples.en: The child asks where Mom is.
She asks me to help her.

related.en: to ask, to request — that someone do something: «проси́ть о по́мощи»

note: «Спра́шивать» asks for information. To ask someone to do something, use «проси́ть»: «попроси́ его́ помо́чь» (ask him to help).

examples.en: I always take an umbrella with me.
Take my pen.

related.en: to take (impf.) — repeated or ongoing: «брать с собо́й»

note: «Брать» is imperfective, «взять» perfective: «возьми́ ключи́» (take the keys, once), «всегда́ бери́ ключи́» (always take the keys).

examples.en: Are you going? So am I.
He knows English, and German as well.

related.en: also, as well — adds to a list, more formal

note: «То́же» means «me too, he too»: «я то́же люблю́ ко́фе». «Та́кже» just adds: «я люблю́ ко́фе, а та́кже чай».

examples.en: He is still asleep.
We are already home.

note: «Ещё не» means «not yet», «уже́ не» means «no longer»: «он ещё не пришёл» (he hasn't come yet), «его́ уже́ нет» (he is no longer here).

examples.en: I can't talk right now.

examples.ru: Раньше он жил в Москве, а [тепе́рь] живёт в Казани.
examples.en: He used to live in Moscow, and now he lives in Kazan.

related.en: now, right now; also «in a moment»
now, from now on — in contrast to before

note: «Я сейча́с приду́» means «I'll be right there». «Тепе́рь» always implies a change: it was different before, now it is like this.

examples.en: He worked all day.
I ate a whole watermelon.

related.en: all, the whole — everything of a known whole: «весь го́род»
whole, entire — a complete piece or a large amount: «це́лый час»; also intact

note: «Весь/вся/всё/все» means all of a known whole: «вся семья́». «Це́лый» stresses a complete piece or amount: «це́лая пи́цца», «це́лый час». It also means intact: «це́лая ча́шка».

examples.en: Where do you live?
Where are you going?

related.en: where — the place where someone or something is
where to — the direction of movement

note: With verbs of motion use «куда́», not «где»: «куда́ ты идёшь?». «Отку́да» means «from where».

examples.en: I'm here, waiting for you.
Come here and have a look!
My friends live there.
We are going there by train.

note: Russian has separate words for motion: «иди́ сюда́» (come here), «я е́ду туда́» (I'm going there). «Здесь» and «там» are for being in a place.

examples.en: I have to go.
You need to rest.

related.en: need to, have to — colloquial, the person in the dative: «мне на́до идти́»
necessary, need — somewhat stricter; the adjective «ну́жный» means «needed»

note: Both take the dative and an infinitive. For a thing that is needed, «ну́жный» is usual: «мне нужна́ ва́ша по́мощь» (I need your help).

examples.en: The kids are playing soccer in the yard.
My brother plays the guitar.

related.en: to play a game or sport, with acc. — игра́ть в футбо́л, в ша́хматы
to play an instrument, with prep. — игра́ть на гита́ре, на пиани́но

note: The preposition decides: в + acc. for games and sports, на + prep. for instruments.

examples.en: My brother got married last year.
She married a doctor.
They got married in May.

related.en: to get married (of a man) — жени́ться на + prep.
to get married (of a woman) — вы́йти за́муж за + acc.
to get married (of both) — они́ пожени́лись

note: There is no single verb for both sexes: a man жени́ться, a woman вы́йти за́муж. The state is said differently: он жена́т, она́ за́мужем.

examples.en: I want to eat.
Please, help yourself!

related.en: to eat — the general, neutral verb: я ем
to eat, politely — when offering food to a guest or a child

note: About yourself say я ем: я ку́шаю sounds overly refined. Ку́шать is for inviting someone else: ку́шай, ку́шайте.

examples.en: Show me a different jacket, please.
He lives on the second floor.

related.en: second in order, next in a series — второ́й день

note: If you count in order, say второ́й: второ́й день is the second day in a row. If you mean «some other», say друго́й: друго́й день is a different day.

examples.en: That was the last bus.
He lives in the last house at the end of the street.

related.en: last in time or in a sequence — после́дний раз
outermost, at the very edge — кра́йний дом

note: Кра́йний marks the outermost place in space. In a queue people colloquially ask кто кра́йний? - who is last? For the end of a period of time use после́дний раз.

examples.en: I remember that day well.
We often think back on our student years.
He reminds me of my brother.

related.en: to remember, to keep in mind — a state: я по́мню его́
to recall, to bring back to mind — вспомина́ть де́тство
to remind someone of something; to resemble

examples.en: He is finishing school this year.
We finish work at six.

note: Ко́нчить with no object («я ко́нчил») can be understood as vulgar, so when in doubt say зако́нчить.

examples.en: We live in an old house.
An elderly man was sitting on the bus.

related.en: old — of things and of people
elderly, getting on in years — a polite word for a person

note: Ста́рый said of a person can sound rude, so for a polite word use пожило́й. Ста́рый друг is «an old friend», not «an old man».

examples.en: He is a very kind person.
All people are different.
There were five people in the room.

note: The plural of челове́к is лю́ди, not «человеки». With five and more the counted form is челове́к: пять челове́к, but два челове́ка.

examples.en: We have one child.
Our children go to school.

note: The plural of ребёнок is де́ти. Two is два ребёнка, but five is пять дете́й. Ребя́та also means «guys, folks»: ребя́та, пойдёмте!

examples.en: He is the man who helped me.
What's the date today?

related.en: who, which in a relative clause; which in order
what kind of, which of several — in a question about type or choice

note: Кото́рый is «who, which» in a relative clause (челове́к, кото́рый звони́л); како́й asks «what kind of» or «which» (како́й фильм?). «What time is it?» is Кото́рый час?.

examples.ru: [Е́сли] у тебя будет время, позвони мне.
examples.en: If you have time, call me.
I don't know whether he will come.

related.en: whether — a question, placed after the word it refers to

note: «I don't know whether he will come» is не зна́ю, придёт ли он, not «если он придёт». Если only means «if».

examples.en: He said that he would come later.
I want you to come.

related.en: that — after verbs of saying and thinking: он сказа́л, что...
so that, to — a wish, purpose or order: хочу́, что́бы...

note: Russian has two words for «that»: что for a fact and что́бы for a wish or purpose. After что́бы the verb takes the past-tense form: хочу́, что́бы ты пришёл.

examples.en: I didn't come because I was sick.
He was sick, so he didn't come.

related.en: so, that's why — gives the result

examples.en: His father is strict and authoritarian.
He is a very respected doctor.

related.en: authoritarian — gives orders and imposes his will
authoritative, respected — trusted for knowledge and standing

note: Авторита́рный is strict and asks nobody, often negative. Авторите́тный is someone trusted for knowledge and reputation, positive.

examples.en: He has an unrequited love.
That is an irresponsible act.

related.en: unanswered, unrequited — nobody answers: безотве́тная любо́вь
irresponsible, with no sense of responsibility

note: «Irresponsible» is безотве́тственный, not безотве́тный. Безотве́тный is said of a love or a plea that gets no answer.

examples.ru: В [бу́дние] дни я встаю в семь.
examples.en: On weekdays I get up at seven.
That is ordinary everyday life.

related.en: working, of a weekday — бу́дний день, по бу́дням

note: Only бу́дний means «weekday» in the calendar. Бу́дничный describes what is everyday and routine, with no link to the calendar.

examples.en: This is my ex-husband.
He is a seasoned man, you won't fool him.
We were remembering the past.

related.en: former, ex- — бы́вший муж, бы́вшая жена́
experienced, seasoned — a man who has seen a lot
bygone, of the past — было́е вре́мя (literary)

note: Бы́вший is «former» and stands before the noun: бы́вший президе́нт. Быва́лый is said of experience, было́й of the distant past.

examples.en: I like to lie in a hot bath.
The towel is in the bathroom.

note: Ва́нная is the room (ва́нная ко́мната), ва́нна is the tub itself. In Russian flats the ва́нная and the туале́т are often two separate rooms.

examples.en: Take a deep breath in.
A heavy sigh was heard.

related.en: inhalation — the air you breathe in
sigh — of sadness, tiredness or relief

note: The verbs go the same way: вдохну́ть is «to breathe in», вздохну́ть is «to sigh».

examples.en: Please fill out the form.
She filled the glass with water.
I want to top up my account.
He added to my answer.

related.en: to fill in an empty space or a form — запо́лнить анке́ту
to fill a container — напо́лнить стака́н
to replenish what has been used up — попо́лнить счёт
to add what is missing, to supplement — допо́лнить отве́т

note: Запо́лнить is for forms and empty spaces, напо́лнить for containers. Попо́лнить is to replenish what was used up: попо́лнить запа́сы.

examples.en: He had a hostile look.
The plane was shot down by an enemy missile.

related.en: hostile, unfriendly in attitude — вражде́бный взгляд
enemy, belonging to the enemy — вра́жеская а́рмия

note: Вражде́бный describes an attitude and feelings (a look, a tone), вра́жеский what belongs to the enemy in a war.

examples.en: I spent a long time choosing a gift.
Citizens elect the president.

related.en: to choose, to pick from what is offered — pf. вы́брать
to elect by vote to an office — pf. избра́ть

note: For a personal choice (a gift, clothes, a route) say выбира́ть. Избира́ть is voting: вы́боры are «elections».

examples.en: I paid for lunch.
You can pay the bill by card.
I paid the fine at the bank.
The company paid the salary on time.

related.en: to pay for something you received — заплати́ть за обе́д
to pay a bill or a service — оплати́ть счёт
to pay in to an account, at a bank or cashier — уплати́ть штраф
to pay out a salary, pension or debt — вы́платить зарпла́ту

note: When you pay: заплати́ть, оплати́ть, уплати́ть. When a company or the state pays out: вы́платить - вы́платить пе́нсию.

examples.en: They raised three children.
He decided to grow a beard.
The athlete wants to build up muscle.

related.en: to raise a child, to grow a plant — вы́растить ребёнка
to let hair or a beard grow — отрасти́ть бо́роду
to build up, to increase — нарасти́ть мы́шцы

note: With no object, when something just grows, use вы́расти: он вы́рос - he grew up.

examples.en: The company submitted its annual report.
He signed up for a one-year course.
We have a one-year-old son.

related.en: annual, for the whole year — годово́й отчёт

note: Annual leave is ежего́дный о́тпуск, not годово́й о́тпуск.

examples.en: This is an effective medicine.
Do you have a valid ticket?
The law in force prohibits this.

related.en: operating, working, in force — де́йствующий зако́н

note: The verb is де́йствовать: лека́рство де́йствует - the medicine works. The adverb действи́тельно means «really, indeed».

examples.en: I have a business meeting today.
You gave sound advice.

related.en: business, work-related — делова́я встре́ча, делово́й костю́м

note: Both come from де́ло but are not mixed up: делово́й is about business, де́льный about something being sensible and useful.

examples.en: There is a long corridor here.
A long flight awaits us.

related.en: lasting, prolonged, rather formal — дли́тельный перелёт

note: «Long» is дли́нный for space and дли́тельный for lasting time. In speech до́лгий is more common for time: до́лгий разгово́р.

examples.en: We had a frank, confidential talk.
Children are very trusting.

note: Дове́рчивый is a trait of a person who believes easily and so is easy to deceive. Довери́тельный describes a relationship or tone in which people trust each other.

examples.en: The autumn was rainy this year.
We collected rainwater.

related.en: rain-, coming from rain — дождева́я вода́
rainy, with a lot of rain — дождли́вый день

note: Only дождли́вый means «full of rain»: дождли́вое ле́то. Дождево́й is the adjective of дождь: дождево́й червь - earthworm.

examples.en: That was friendly advice.
Russia and Serbia are friendly countries.
We have a close-knit family.

note: Дру́жный is not «friendly» but «united, harmonious»: a дру́жная кома́нда works together without quarrels.

examples.en: He is our only son.

examples.ru: В Москве есть [еди́ный] билет на метро и автобус.
examples.en: In Moscow there is a single ticket for the metro and the bus.
The prisoner is in a solitary cell.

related.en: single, unified as a whole — еди́ный биле́т

note: Еди́нственный means «the only one», not «unique» in the sense of exceptional: that is уника́льный.

examples.en: You are our welcome guest.
Today it is advisable to wear a warm jacket.

note: Жела́тельно is often used as an impersonal word: жела́тельно прийти́ - it is advisable to come.

examples.en: He is a cruel man.
The mattress is too hard.

related.en: hard, stiff; strict, harsh — жёсткая крова́ть

note: Жёсткий is hard (жёсткое мя́со - tough meat) and strict (жёсткие усло́вия - harsh terms), жесто́кий is cruel.

examples.en: He is a skilled cook.
These are artificial flowers.

note: Both come from иску́сство («art, skill»): иску́сный is skillful, иску́сственный is man-made.

examples.en: What a boor! He didn't even say hello.
He is a complete ignoramus in music.

note: A memory aid: неве́жа lacks politeness (ве́жливый), неве́жда lacks knowledge (ве́дать).

examples.en: The toothache became unbearable.
He is very impatient.

examples.ru: У него [нетерпи́мое] отношение к чужому мнению.
examples.en: He is intolerant of other people's opinions.

note: A memory aid: нетерпели́вый can't wait, нестерпи́мый hurts, нетерпи́мый does not accept.

examples.en: Today is a very successful day.
He is a very lucky person.

related.en: successful, well chosen — уда́чный день, уда́чная шу́тка

note: «Happy» in the sense of joyful is счастли́вый, not уда́чный; уда́ча is «luck».

examples.en: We discussed the plan for tomorrow.
The court sentenced him to two years.

related.en: to discuss, to talk over — обсуди́ть пла́ны
to condemn, to sentence — осуди́ть на два го́да

note: Do not mix them up: обсуди́ть is to discuss, осуди́ть is to sentence or to blame. Likewise обсужде́ние - discussion, осужде́ние - condemnation.

examples.en: He can't tell truth from lies.
It is hard to tell colors apart in the dark.

related.en: to distinguish one thing from another — отлича́ть оригина́л от ко́пии
to make out, to see the difference — различа́ть цвета́

note: «To differ from» is отлича́ться от + gen.: она́ отлича́ется от сестры́. Различа́ть is «to make out, tell apart», as in различа́ть цвета́.

examples.en: The explanation was very clear.
He is a quick student.

related.en: quick, bright, grasps things fast — поня́тливый учени́к

note: Поня́тно! in conversation means «I see, got it».

examples.en: That was a brave act.
He was fired for such a misdemeanor.

note: A court case is not посту́пок but проце́сс. Посту́пок is a person's act, просту́пок is a minor offense of theirs.

examples.en: He lived to a venerable age.
He answered in a respectful tone.
He was the guest of honor at the celebration.

note: Почётный is «honorary»: почётный гражданин. Почти́тельный shows respect, while почте́нный is someone who deserves it.

examples.en: There were salads on the festive table.
Don't ask idle questions.

note: Пра́здный means «idle, pointless», not «festive»; «holiday» is пра́здник.

examples.en: We have a practical class today.
The bag is very practical.

related.en: relating to practice, as opposed to theory — практи́ческая рабо́та
useful and easy to use — практи́чная вещь

note: English «practical» covers both: практи́ческий is «from practice», практи́чный is «easy to use».

examples.en: The company provided me with an apartment.
Allow me to introduce my friend to you.

related.en: to provide, to make available — предоста́вить кварти́ру
to introduce someone; to imagine — предста́вить дру́га

note: Предста́вить also means «to imagine»: предста́вь себе́ - imagine. Предоста́вить is «to provide» a right, lodging or time.

examples.en: This is a very hearty lunch.
I'm already full.

related.en: full, having eaten enough — я сыт

note: A dish or meal is сы́тный; a person who has eaten enough is сыт.

examples.en: He is a very humane boss.
That is a human error.

related.en: humane, kind to people — челове́чное отноше́ние
human, relating to people — челове́ческая жизнь

note: Челове́чный is someone who behaves kindly and warmly, челове́ческий is everything that belongs to a human being: челове́ческая приро́да.

examples.en: He studies economics.
This will save time.

related.en: economy; the science of economics — росси́йская эконо́мика
saving, economy of resources — эконо́мия вре́мени

note: «A saving» is эконо́мия, and «to save» is эконо́мить: эконо́мить де́ньги.

examples.en: An economic crisis began in the country.
We have an economical car.
My mom is very thrifty.

related.en: economical, cheap to run — экономи́чная маши́на
thrifty, frugal (of a person) — эконо́мный челове́к

note: The adjective of эконо́мика is only экономи́ческий. Экономи́чный and эконо́мный come from эконо́мия.

examples.en: This is an effective way.
She is wearing a striking dress.

related.en: striking, makes a strong impression by its looks — эффе́ктная вне́шность

note: Эффекти́вный is judged by results, эффе́ктный by looks.

examples.en: We moved to a neighboring town.
The neighbor's dog had puppies.

related.en: the neighbor's, belonging to a neighbor — сосе́дская соба́ка

note: Сосе́дний is what lies next to you (сосе́дняя ко́мната), сосе́дский what belongs to the су́сед.

examples.en: The match was played at an ice arena.
An icy wind is blowing outside.

related.en: ice-, of ice, in names and sports — ледо́вая аре́на

note: Ледяно́й is said of what is as cold as ice or made of ice, also ледяно́й взгляд. Ледо́вый is for names: ледо́вый дворе́ц.

examples.ru: Он мой лучший [друг], мы вместе с детства.
examples.en: He is my best friend, we have been together since childhood.

examples.ru: Это не друг, а просто [прия́тель] с работы.
examples.en: He's not a real friend, just a buddy from work.

related.en: close friend — someone you can count on
buddy, pal — someone you get on with, but not necessarily close

note: Друг is a stronger word than «friend»: you call someone друг only if he is really close. A casual friend is прия́тель.

examples.en: What is your surname? - Petrova.
There are four people in our family.

note: A trap: фами́лия is only a surname, never «family». Relatives, the extended family, are родня́.

examples.ru: Девочка заплела [косу́] и пошла в школу.
examples.en: The girl braided her hair and went to school.
She has long dark hair.

related.en: hair on the head — used only in the plural

note: A single hair is «во́лос». The saying «нашла́ коса́ на ка́мень» (literally "the scythe hit a stone") means that two stubborn sides have met their match.

examples.en: I added cinnamon to the pie.
Kids love the crust of fresh bread.
A pine tree has thick bark.

related.en: crust, rind — of bread, cheese, a lemon
bark — of a tree; also the cortex in anatomy

examples.en: You can't use your phone during the lesson.
The train arrived on time.

related.en: during — a preposition, followed by the genitive

note: Two words is a preposition with a noun (во вре́мя обе́да), one word is an adverb meaning «on time». In speech the stress tells them apart.

examples.en: A thunderstorm is forecast for tonight.
Thunder is rumbling in the distance.
Lightning struck a tree.

related.en: thunderstorm — a storm with thunder and lightning

examples.en: My uncle told a funny joke.
Don't be offended, it was just a joke.

related.en: joke — a short funny story with a punchline, told to entertain
joke, jest — something said or done for fun

note: Not an «anecdote»: анекдо́т is a told joke. A true story about an event is «забавная исто́рия».

examples.en: We have fast internet at home.
Don't be so sly, tell me honestly!
You play the guitar really well!
Hey, Seryoga! How's it going?

related.en: hi, hey (colloq., among friends) — Здорово́, друг!

note: Only the stress tells these words apart. Здорово́ is a greeting between close people; to older people say «здра́вствуйте».

examples.en: The pharmacy is open around the clock.

examples.ru: Поезд идёт до Москвы почти двое [су́ток].
examples.en: The train takes almost two days and nights to get to Moscow.
In winter the day is short and the night is long.

related.en: a 24-hour period, day and night together — круглые су́тки
day, the daylight part; also a calendar day — день рожде́ния

note: Су́тки has only a plural: двое су́ток, пять су́ток. English has no single word for it: «24 hours» is the closest.

examples.en: We need some rest in the fresh air.
He took his vacation in August.
The children's winter break has started.
I have a day off on Saturday.

related.en: rest, relaxation in general — хоро́ший о́тдых
vacation, leave from work — уйти́ в о́тпуск
school or university break — зи́мние кани́кулы
day off from work — рабо́тать без выходны́х

note: Кани́кулы has no singular. «On break» is «на кани́кулах».

examples.en: He raised his glass to our health.
Put the carafe of water on the table.
There's a little compote left in the pitcher.

related.en: stemmed glass, wine glass — бока́л вина
carafe, a glass bottle with a stopper for water or juice — графи́н воды
pitcher, jug with a handle — кувши́н молока

examples.en: He fell and bruised his buttocks.
Models often have high cheekbones.
The girl has rosy cheeks.
We got very tired after the hike.
Tomorrow I have to get up at six.

related.en: to get tired — уста́ть от рабо́ты; impf. устава́ть
to get up, stand up — вста́ть ра́но; impf. встава́ть

note: Уста́ть means «to get tired»: я уста́л is «I'm tired».

examples.en: They say a ghost lives in this house.
A ghost appeared in the castle at night.
The team has not lost its fighting spirit.

related.en: spirit — inner strength, morale — боево́й дух
ghost, specter; also figurative — при́зрак войны́

examples.en: We'll be there soon.
I've almost finished the report.
I got back from vacation recently.

related.en: recently, not long ago — неда́вно ви́дел

examples.en: I don't know this man.
- Are you hungry? - No, thank you.
I don't have time.

related.en: not — before a verb, adjective or adverb — я не рабо́таю
no (as an answer); there is no, I have no — у меня́ нет сестры́

note: Before a verb use only «не» (я не рабо́таю). «Нет» is the answer «no» and also «there is no / I have no». Wrong: «я нет работаю», «у меня не сестры».

examples.en: I bought new fins for diving.
Swallows fly back to us in spring.

related.en: flipper, fin (of a diver, seal, penguin) — ла́сты для плавания
swallow, the bird — ла́сточка в небе

note: Ла́сточка is also a term of endearment: «ла́сточка моя́».

examples.en: A button came off the shirt.
Press the doorbell button.

related.en: push button, one you press — of a doorbell, elevator, phone, appliance

note: Кно́пка is also a snap fastener on a jacket or pillowcase.

meanings: eraser or rubber band: ластик or резинка?

examples.en: I erased the mistake with an eraser.
I tie my hair in a ponytail with a hair tie.

related.en: eraser, for rubbing out pencil — купить ла́стик и каранда́ш
elastic band, hair tie, rubber band — рези́нка для воло́с, канцеля́рская рези́нка

note: In speech рези́нка can also mean an eraser, so you will be understood. But a hair tie is never «ла́стик».

examples.en: The glasses are in the case.
Buy a case for your phone.

related.en: case, a hard box or holder shaped to the object — for glasses, a violin
cover, a soft slip-on case — for a phone, furniture, a car seat

note: A gun holster is «ко́бура».

meanings: cake: калач, торт, пирожное or пирог?

examples.en: Mom baked a cake for my birthday.
Pastries were served with tea.
Grandma is baking an apple pie.

examples.ru: В городе до сих пор пекут [калачи́].
examples.en: They still bake kalachi in the town, a white bread of a traditional shape.

related.en: cake — a large cake, for a birthday or celebration
pastry — an individual small cake, e.g. an eclair — пиро́жное с кре́мом
pie — baked dough with a filling, sweet or savory
kalach — a traditional white wheat bread of a special shape, not a sweet cake

note: Cookies and biscuits are «пече́нье», and a small filled bun is «пирожо́к».

examples.en: He dreams of fame as an actor.
It's Nina's name day today.
They invited all their relatives to the christening.

related.en: fame, glory — a reputation, not a celebration
name day — the feast day of the saint whose name you bear, celebrated by the individual
christening, baptism — the celebration for a baptized child

examples.en: I need a thread and a needle.
The dentist recommends using dental floss.
The film is coming to an end.

related.en: end — коне́ц фильма; not a thread
thread, for sewing — ни́тка с игло́й
thread, filament — зубная нить (floss), нить жаро́вки, нить расска́за (the thread of a story)

examples.ru: Напиши на конверте [и́ндекс], без него письмо задержится.
examples.en: Write the postal code on the envelope, or the letter will be delayed.
The student put his record book on the table.

related.en: postal code, ZIP code; also a numerical indicator, e.g. a price index
student record book (colloq. for зачётная книжка)

examples.ru: На ферме у них три [ло́шади] и две коровы.
examples.en: They have three horses and two cows on the farm.
A white horse raced across the field.
This mare will foal soon.

related.en: horse — the general, ordinary word for either sex
steed, horse — as a riding animal; poetic; also the chess knight (шахматный конь)

note: In everyday speech «horse» is usually ло́шадь; конь sounds more elevated.

examples.en: Why did you buy so much bread?
Why didn't you come yesterday?

related.en: why, what for — asks about a purpose
why, for what reason — asks about a cause

note: English «why» covers both. If you could ask «what for?», use заче́м; the answer goes with что́бы. If you ask «for what reason?», use почему́; the answer goes with потому́ что.

examples.en: I did nothing all day.
I have nothing to wear tonight.
There's nothing to eat in the fridge.

related.en: nothing — goes with не and a finite verb
nothing to (do, eat, wear) — goes with an infinitive

note: The stress differs: ничего́, but не́чего. «I'm not reading anything» is я ничего́ не чита́ю, while «I have nothing to read» is мне не́чего чита́ть.

examples.en: The weather is nice today.
What a pretty hairstyle she has!
Have a nice day!

related.en: beautiful, pretty — pleasing to the eye or ear: a face, a dress, a city, a song
good, nice — pleasant, favorable: weather, a day, news, a vacation

note: English «nice» often matches хоро́ший, not краси́вый: nice weather is хоро́шая пого́да, a nice day is хоро́ший день, and «to ask nicely» is хорошо́ попроси́ть.

examples.en: We danced until morning yesterday.
The children are dancing around the Christmas tree.

related.en: to dance — neutral, any dance (waltz, tango)
to dance — colloquial, a folk or lively dance

note: Two verbs for «to dance». They also differ in form: я танцу́ю, but я пляшу́, ты пля́шешь.

examples.en: I eat everything except fish.
These pills are for a headache.

related.en: except, apart from — introduces the exception: все, кроме Ани
from; for, against — where something comes from or what it protects against: письмо от брата, лекарство от кашля

note: Only кро́ме introduces an exception. Both prepositions take the genitive.

examples.en: My name is Igor.
They named their daughter Anna.
What is this street called?

related.en: to call: меня зовут - my name is (for people and pets); звать в гости - to invite
to name, give a name: называть сына Антоном (instr.)
to be called, for things and places: a cafe, a film, a book

note: A person's name stays in the nominative: меня зовут Мария. After назвать the name is in the instrumental: назвали Марией. For things never «зову́т», only называ́ется.

examples.en: In winter I wear a warm hat.
On the beach she put on a wide-brimmed hat.
He bought a new cap for running.

related.en: winter hat — knitted or fur; the шапка-ушанка has ear flaps
cap with a visor, a summer cap

note: The шапка-уша́нка has «ears» («уши») that fold down in the cold.

examples.en: He speaks Russian with a slight accent.

examples.ru: В этом слове [ударе́ние] падает на первый слог.
examples.en: In this word the stress falls on the first syllable.

related.en: accent — a foreign accent in pronunciation: говорить с акцентом; also emphasis: сделать акцент на чём-то
stress — the stressed syllable of a word: поставить ударение

note: Stress is «placed» in Russian: поста́вьте ударе́ние.

examples.en: Our professor gives lectures at the university.

examples.ru: Мой [учи́тель] русского языка вышел на пенсию.
examples.en: My Russian teacher has retired.
She works as a lecturer at the institute.

related.en: professor — a university rank, a senior title
teacher in a primary or secondary school
instructor, lecturer — at a college, an institute or a course

note: Профе́ссор is only a high university rank, not a school teacher. A school teacher is учи́тель and is addressed by first name and patronymic.

examples.ru: Вчера мы посмотрели весь [сериа́л] за вечер.
examples.en: Yesterday we watched the whole series in one evening.
I liked the last episode.

related.en: TV series as a whole, with all its episodes (masc.)
one episode; also a set: серия марок (fem.)

note: A сериа́л consists of many се́рий: в сериа́ле мно́го се́рий.

examples.en: I add a spoonful of sour cream to the borscht.
She poured cream into her coffee.

related.en: sour cream — with borscht, dumplings, pelmeni
cream (sweet) — for coffee and for whipping (plural only)

note: Whipped cream is «взби́тые сли́вки». Сли́вки exists only in the plural.

examples.en: After lunch I wash the dishes.
Pour the water into a plastic container.
Blood flows through the blood vessels.

related.en: dishes, tableware as a whole: plates, cups, pots (singular only)
container — one vessel for liquid, tank
vessel — in formal style and in anatomy: кровено́сный сосу́д

note: Посу́да means «dishes» as a whole. One dish or container is not посу́да but ёмкость, or colloquially посу́дина.

examples.ru: На [у́треннике] в саду дети читали стихи.
examples.en: At the kindergarten party the children recited poems.
The teacher wrote a remark in the school diary.
Leave the night light on, the child is afraid of the dark.

related.en: children's party at kindergarten or school — not a morning
diary; also a pupil's school notebook for homework and grades
night light, a small lamp that stays on at night — not the night

note: The roots look familiar, but do not guess the meaning from у́тро, день, ночь.

examples.en: Uncle Vitya is my godfather.

examples.ru: Лучшая подруга станет [свиде́тельницей] на нашей свадьбе.
examples.en: My best friend will be our witness at the wedding.

related.en: godfather (godmother: крёстная) — holds the child at the baptism
wedding witness (female: свиде́тельница) — signs the marriage register

examples.ru: Мы зашли в [собо́р] и поставили свечи.
examples.en: We went into the cathedral and lit candles.
Tomorrow there's a parents' meeting at school.

related.en: cathedral, a large church (Исаа́киевский собо́р); also a church council
meeting, assembly — of a building's residents, of a school

examples.ru: Купи мне [любо́й] хлеб, мне всё равно.
examples.en: Buy me any bread, I don't care which.
Every day he walks the dog.
This store sells all sorts of toys.

related.en: any, whichever — one by free choice: любо́й день
all kinds of, various (mostly plural): вся́кие книги
each, every — individually, one by one: ка́ждый ребёнок

note: Trap: вся́кие игрушки is not «all toys» but «all sorts of toys». For «every», use ка́ждый; вся́кий in the singular (вся́кий зна́ет) sounds bookish.

examples.en: I left my gloves at home, my hands are freezing.
Grandma knitted me warm mittens.
Ded Moroz (Grandfather Frost) came in red mittens.

related.en: gloves — with separate fingers: ordinary, leather, work, boxing
mittens — knitted, with a single thumb and no separate fingers
mittens, mitts — thick, without separate fingers, often work gloves; sounds old-fashioned

note: Boxing gloves are «боксёрские перча́тки», not рукави́цы.

examples.en: The bishop moves only diagonally.
He put his rook on the open file.
I lost my queen and lost the game.
The knight moves in an L shape.

related.en: rook — moves along straight lines; ладья́ is also an old word for a boat
bishop — moves diagonally; слон is also the animal, an elephant
knight — moves in an L shape; конь is also a horse

note: Do not translate these literally: слон («elephant») is the bishop, конь («horse») is the knight, ладья́ is the rook. King and pawn are the plain ones: коро́ль, пе́шка.

examples.ru: Для теста нужны мука, вода и [дро́жжи].
examples.en: Dough needs flour, water and yeast.

examples.ru: Летом в жару хорошо выпить холодного [ква́са].
examples.en: In the summer heat it's nice to drink cold kvass.

related.en: yeast — for dough, bread and beer (plural only)
kvass — a refreshing drink made from rye bread; not yeast

note: Дро́жжи is plural only: све́жие дро́жжи (fresh yeast), сухи́е дро́жжи (dry yeast).

examples.en: First whisk the eggs with the sugar.

examples.ru: Не [мути́] воду, я хочу видеть дно.
examples.en: Don't muddy the water, I want to see the bottom.

related.en: to make cloudy, to muddy: мути́ть во́ду; меня́ мути́т - I feel sick
to whisk, beat — eggs, cream: взбить яйца́

note: To whisk eggs or cream, use взбить, not мутить.

examples.en: She's in a good mood today.

examples.ru: Мне не нравится [расположе́ние] комнат в этой квартире.
examples.en: I don't like the layout of the rooms in this apartment.
He won his boss's favor.

related.en: layout, location (of rooms, buildings); also favor, goodwill: добиться расположения

note: «Not in the mood» is нет настрое́ния.

examples.ru: В музее висит большая [карти́на] с морем.
examples.en: A big painting of the sea hangs in the museum.
My son brought a drawing home from school.
Send me your photo.

related.en: painting — a picture as a work of art, e.g. oil on canvas
drawing — in pencil, marker or crayons; also a pattern on fabric
photograph — a picture taken with a camera or phone

note: The verb depends on the tool: фотографи́ровать with a camera, рисова́ть with a pencil, писа́ть карти́ну (literally «to write») with paints.

examples.en: Turn on the speaker, let's listen to some music.

examples.ru: В телефоне сломался [дина́мик], я ничего не слышу.
examples.en: The speaker in my phone is broken, I can't hear anything.
The tourists walked in a column along the embankment.

related.en: speaker — a standalone one; also a newspaper column, and a gas pump
speaker — built into a phone, laptop or car
column, pillar; also a column of people or vehicles

note: A standalone speaker is коло́нка; the one inside a phone is дина́мик.

examples.en: Spread a clean cloth on the table.
It's time to change the baby's diaper.
The baby was dressed in a little shirt and rompers.

related.en: cloth diaper, flat baby cloth — the baby is wrapped in it or it is laid under him
disposable diaper, Pampers — goes on the baby's bottom
baby's shirt, undershirt — opens at the front

note: English «diaper» covers both cloth and disposable; Russian tells them apart. So «change the diaper» is usually поменя́ть подгу́зник, not пелёнку.

examples.ru: В июле в городе стоит страшная [жара́].
examples.en: There's terrible heat in the city in July.
He spoke with great passion.
The child has a fever, we need to call a doctor.

related.en: heat — intense hot weather outside — Любите жару́?
heat, glow; embers; figuratively fervor; also a sick person's fever

note: They are not the same word: жара́ is feminine (gen. жары́), жар is masculine (gen. жа́ра). A sick person's fever is often жар.

examples.en: Add a pinch of black pepper to the soup.

examples.ru: В салат я кладу помидоры и сладкий [пе́рец].
examples.en: I put tomatoes and sweet pepper in the salad.
Sprinkle the meat with paprika.

related.en: pepper — on its own, black pepper; with an adjective also the vegetable — чёрный пе́рец (black pepper), болга́рский пе́рец (bell pepper), о́стрый пе́рец (hot pepper)
paprika — mainly the ground spice; the vegetable is usually called болга́рский пе́рец

note: A bell pepper (the vegetable) is болга́рский пе́рец. The word пе́рец alone can mean several things, so the adjective decides which is meant.

examples.en: Slice the cheese and put it on the bread.

examples.ru: На завтрак я ем [творо́г] со сметаной.
examples.en: For breakfast I eat tvorog with sour cream.
You need fresh tvorog for syrniki.

related.en: cheese — firm or semi-hard, aged: on bread, in a sandwich
tvorog, cottage cheese — fresh, crumbly curd cheese, for breakfast, syrniki, pies

note: Сы́рники (cheese pancakes) are made from творо́г, not сыр.

examples.ru: На завтрак мама пожарила [блины́] с джемом.
examples.en: For breakfast Mom fried crepes with jam.
I like oladyi with sour cream.

related.en: blin — a thin crepe-like pancake, poured over the whole pan, often folded or filled
oladya — a small thick pancake, like an American pancake, from kefir or sour milk batter spooned into the pan

note: Batter spooned into the pan that turns out small and thick makes ола́дьи. Блины́ are thin, like crepes.

examples.en: The pot is on the stove.
Put the soup on the small burner.
The pie is still in the oven.

related.en: stove, cooker — the whole appliance (gas, electric) — кухо́нная плита́
burner — one ring on the stove
oven — the baking compartment of the stove

note: A pot goes на плиту́ or на конфо́рку, a pie goes в духо́вку.

meanings: уживаться, наслаждаться, получать удовольствие or кайфовать?

examples.en: The cat doesn't get along with the dog.

examples.ru: Мы весь день [наслажда́лись] морем и тишиной.
examples.en: We enjoyed the sea and the quiet all day.
I enjoy this music.
Yesterday we chilled out on the beach and really enjoyed ourselves.

related.en: to get along, live in harmony — уживаться с соседом
to enjoy, delight in something (+ instr.) — наслаждаться музыкой
to enjoy, take pleasure in (от + gen.) — получать удовольствие от работы
to enjoy oneself, chill (colloq.) — кайфовать на море

note: Ужива́ться means «to get along with someone», not «to enjoy». The other three are the verbs for «to enjoy».

examples.en: There was cherry kisel, a thick sweet fruit drink, for dessert.
In the morning I drink prostokvasha, soured milk, with bread.
Ryazhenka is made from baked milk.

related.en: kisel — a thick sweet drink of fruit juice and starch, warm or cold — клюквенный кисель
prostokvasha — soured milk, a bit like thin yogurt — стакан простокваши
ryazhenka — fermented baked milk with a mild caramel taste — ряженка с булочкой

note: Кисе́ль is not sour at all: it is sweet and thick.

examples.en: My daughter is in fifth grade.
He was admitted to the surgical department.

related.en: class, grade; the pupils of one grade; also a classroom — учи́ться в пя́том кла́ссе
department, section or branch of an institution — отделе́ние по́чты, поли́ции, больни́цы

note: A pupil is asked «в како́м ты кла́ссе?»; the answer is a number and a letter, e.g. в пя́том «Б».

examples.en: She put red lipstick on her lips.
Put ointment on the burn, it will heal quickly.

examples.ru: Купи [крем] для рук, у меня кожа сухая.
examples.en: Buy some hand cream, my skin is dry.

related.en: lipstick — губна́я пома́да; also hair pomade
ointment, salve — medicinal: мазь от ожо́гов
cream — skin cream; also the cream filling of a cake — крем для лица́

note: Пома́да is only for lips and hair; a medicinal ointment is мазь.

examples.en: She is Russian but lives in Belgrade.

examples.ru: У него [росси́йский] паспорт, хотя он татарин.
examples.en: He has a Russian passport, although he is a Tatar.

related.en: Russian by ethnicity and language — ру́сский язы́к, ру́сская культу́ра
Russian by state, of Russia — росси́йский паспорт, росси́йские зако́ны

note: English «Russian» covers both. A citizen of Russia is a россия́нин even if not ру́сский, for example a Tatar or a Chechen.

cyr: Going in Russian: идти or ехать

examples.en: I'm walking to the store.
Tomorrow we're going to Moscow.

related.en: to go by transport: car, train, bus

note:
English «to go» corresponds to two Russian verbs:
• идти́ - on foot
• е́хать - by any kind of transport

So «I'm going to Belgrade» by train is я е́ду в Белгра́д, not я иду́ в Белгра́д.

The same goes for ходи́ть and е́здить: «I travel often» is я ча́сто е́зжу.

cyr: Russian has no «is» in the present tense

examples.en: He is a doctor.
We are at home.

related.en: to be; left out in the present tense

note:
Russian has no verb быть («is», «am», «are») in the present tense, so the sentence goes without it.

• Он врач. - He is a doctor.
• Где ты? - Where are you?
• Мы до́ма. - We are at home.
• Э́то кни́га. - This is a book.

The verb comes back only in the past and the future: он был врачо́м, он бу́дет врачо́м.

Between two nouns a dash often stands in writing: Москва́ - столи́ца Росси́и.

cyr: The past tense: one form ending in -л

examples.en: Yesterday I was reading until late at night.
Mom came home at seven.

note:
The Russian past tense has one form, made with the ending -л, and no auxiliary verb (nothing like «was» or «have»).

The ending shows gender and number, and a pronoun shows the person:
• я чита́л, я чита́ла - I read, I was reading (man, woman)
• ты чита́л, ты чита́ла - you read (man, woman)
• он чита́л, она́ чита́ла, оно́ чита́ло - he, she, it read
• мы, вы, они́ чита́ли - we, you, they read

So the pronoun cannot be left out: чита́л alone could mean «I read», «you read» or «he read».

There is no separate past continuous or perfect: this one form covers «I read», «I was reading» and «I have read», and aspect (чита́л, прочита́л) shows whether the action was completed.

cyr: The future: бу́ду or a perfective verb

examples.en: Tomorrow I will be working all day.
Tomorrow I will do it.

related.en: I will read, I will be reading (imperfective)
I will read it through, I will finish reading (perfective)

note:
Russian has no single future ending like English «will». The future is made in two ways:

1. imperfective verb: бу́ду + infinitive - я бу́ду де́лать (I will be doing)
2. perfective verb: the present-tense form has a future meaning - я сде́лаю (I will do it, I will get it done)

A perfective verb is never used with бу́ду: «я бу́ду сде́лать» is wrong.

So «I will read it through» is я прочита́ю, and «I will be reading (for a long time, regularly)» is я бу́ду чита́ть.

cyr: что́бы: «want you to...» and «in order to»

examples.en: I want you to come.
Mom asked us to help.

related.en: so that, in order to (also after «want», «ask»: «want you to»)

note:
When the second verb has a different subject («I want you to come», «she asks us to help»), Russian uses что́бы + the past-tense form, not an infinitive as in English.

• Хочу́, что́бы ты пришёл. - I want you to come.
• Она́ про́сит, что́бы мы помогли́. - She asks us to help.

The verb has a past-tense form, but it does not refer to the past: the action is yet to happen.

When the subject is the same, что́бы is not used: хочу́ уйти́ (I want to leave).

Что́бы also means «in order to»: Я учу́ ру́сский, что́бы свобо́дно говори́ть - I'm studying Russian in order to speak fluently.

cyr: To have: у меня́ есть and у меня́ нет

examples.en: I have a sister.
We don't have any time.

related.en: there is, there exists (у меня есть = I have)

note:
Russian has no verb «to have» in this sense. «I have a brother» is said with «у» + gen. and «есть»:

• «У меня́ есть брат.» - I have a brother (literally: at me there is a brother).
• «У нас есть вре́мя.» - We have time.

The thing owned is the subject, and the owner is in the genitive after «у».

Negative: есть becomes нет and the thing owned goes into the genitive: «У меня́ нет бра́та» - I have no brother.

In the past, the form of быть agrees with the thing owned: «у неё была́ сестра́», «у нас бы́ло вре́мя».

The verb име́ть exists, but it sounds bookish.

examples.en: I have no money.
There was no rain yesterday.

note:
After нет, не бы́ло and не бу́дет, the thing that is missing stands in the genitive, not in the nominative:

• «Здесь нет пробле́м.» - There are no problems here.
• «Вчера́ дождя́ не бы́ло.» - There was no rain yesterday.
• «В го́роде нет метро́.» - There is no metro in the city.

So it is not «нет вре́мя», but нет вре́мени.

After не with a transitive verb and a concrete object the accusative usually stays: Я не чита́ю газе́ту. The genitive is more bookish and comes with abstract nouns: не име́ет значе́ния.

cyr: To become, to be, to work as: the instrumental

examples.en: My brother became a doctor.
She works as an engineer.

note:
After «become» and «work as», Russian uses the instrumental, not the nominative.

• стать врачо́м - to become a doctor
• рабо́тать инжене́ром - to work as an engineer
• быть учи́телем - to be a teacher (in the past and future: Он был учи́телем)

The instrumental also follows станови́ться, остава́ться, каза́ться, называ́ться: Он оказа́лся врачо́м - It turned out that he was a doctor.

In the present tense there is no verb, so the nominative stays: Он учи́тель.

cyr: «In» or «at»: в and на with places

examples.en: Mom is at work right now.
The children are at school until two.
I'm going to the post office.

note:
Russian has two prepositions for places, and English «in» or «at» does not tell you which one to use.

• на - рабо́та, по́чта, вокза́л, ста́нция, ры́нок, у́лица, ку́хня: на рабо́те, на по́чте, на вокза́ле
• в - шко́ла, магази́н, больни́ца, кварти́ра, го́род: в шко́ле, в магази́не, в больни́це

Motion toward a place: the same preposition + accusative: на по́чту, на рабо́ту, в шко́лу.

Common mistakes are «в по́чте» and «в рабо́те»: «at the post office» is на по́чте.

There is no rule: learn the preposition together with the word.

examples.en: Mom, we're here!
Misha, come here!

related.en: God! (a relic of the old vocative)

note:
Russian has no vocative case: a person is addressed in the nominative.

• Ма́ша! - Masha!
• Ми́ша, иди́ сюда́! - Misha, come here!

In conversation, names ending in «-а» and «-я» lose that ending, which gives something like a vocative: Маш! Мам! Пап! Ко́ль! Серёж!

This is only for close people and is optional. Relics of the old vocative are Бо́же! and Го́споди!

cyr: Numbers and cases: the traps after 2-4 and 5+

examples.en: I have two sisters.
He is three years old.
I am twenty-five years old.

note:
After a number the noun is in the genitive: singular after 2, 3 and 4, plural after 5 and more. English speakers expect a plain plural, so the details matter.

• два for masculine and neuter, две for feminine: два бра́та, две сестры́
• an adjective after 2-4 is in the genitive plural: два но́вых стола́, but две но́вые кни́ги
• год: два го́да, but пять лет
• пять челове́к, not «челове́ков»
• 21, 31...: оди́н at the end means the noun is singular: два́дцать оди́н стол

cyr: Came, left, went in, went out: prefixed verbs of motion

examples.en: When will you come?
He left the house at seven.
Drop by my place in the evening.

related.en: to drop by, to stop in

note:
Russian makes verbs like «to come», «to leave», «to go in», «to go out», «to cross» and «to pass» from the root -йти and a prefix: прийти́, уйти́, войти́, вы́йти, перейти́, пройти́. They are perfective.

• пришёл, пришла́ - came (m., f.)
• ушёл, ушла́ - left
• вошёл, вошла́ - went in
• вы́шел, вы́шла - went out
• перешёл, прошёл, зашёл - crossed, passed, dropped by

When you travel by vehicle: прие́хать, уе́хать, въе́хать (-е́хать instead of -йти́).

examples.en: He took his own jacket.
He took her jacket.

note:
Unlike мой and твой, the words его́ (his), её (her) and их (their) never change for gender or case.

• его́ сестра́, с его́ сестро́й, о его́ сестре́
• её брат, с её бра́том
• их до́ма (the form «и́хний» is heard, but it is non-standard)

Свой refers back to the subject of the sentence: Он взял свою́ ку́ртку (his own jacket). Он взял её ку́ртку - he took her jacket, someone else's.

Свой changes like мой: свой, своя́, своё, свои́.

cyr: Short adjectives: рад, бо́лен, гото́в, до́лжен

examples.en: I'm very glad to see you.
Mom is busy right now.

note:
Some adjectives have a short form in the predicate: no ending in the masculine, and the gender shows in the ending.

• Я рад. - I'm glad.
• Он бо́лен, она́ больна́. - He is ill, she is ill.
• Он гото́в, она́ гото́ва. - He is ready, she is ready.
• Он до́лжен, она́ должна́. - He must, she must (is obliged to).
• Он за́нят, она́ занята́. - He is busy, she is busy.

After the masculine form the stress often moves: бо́лен, больна́, больно́, больны́. Рад changes like this: рад, ра́да, ра́до, ра́ды.

These forms are not used before a noun: there the full adjective is used.

cyr: The comparative: бо́льше, лу́чше and чем

examples.en: This car is cheaper than that one.
She is two years older than me.

note:
In the predicate the Russian comparative does not change for gender or number and ends in -ее or -е: быстре́е, деше́вле, ста́рше.

• Э́то деше́вле. - This is cheaper.
• Сестра́ ста́рше. - My sister is older.

Comparing:
1. чем + nominative: Он ста́рше, чем я.
2. genitive without чем: Он ста́рше меня́, ста́рше бра́та.

Irregular: хоро́ший - лу́чше, плохо́й - ху́же, мно́го - бо́льше, ма́ло - ме́ньше.

«Much older» is гора́здо ста́рше or намно́го ста́рше, never «о́чень ста́рше».

cyr: Impersonal sentences: мне хо́лодно, мне ну́жно, мо́жно, нельзя́

examples.en: I'm cold.
Smoking is not allowed here.
You need to get some sleep.

note:
Russian expresses a state or a need with an impersonal sentence: the person who feels it is in the dative, and the word with it ends in «-о», with no subject.

• Мне хо́лодно. - I'm cold.
• Ему́ ску́чно. - He is bored.
• Мне на́до, мне ну́жно. - I need to, I have to.
• Мо́жно. - It's allowed, one may.
• Нельзя́. - It's forbidden, one must not.

Past: Мне бы́ло хо́лодно; future: Мне бу́дет хо́лодно.

Note: нельзя́ usually means «not allowed», not «I am unable to»: Мне нельзя́ кури́ть - I'm not allowed to smoke.

cyr: Мне нра́вится: the thing liked is the subject

examples.en: I like this city.
Do you like these movies?
I like you.

note:
Russian turns «I like it» around: the person who likes is in the dative, and the thing liked is the subject, so the verb agrees with it.

• Мне нра́вится э́тот го́род. - I like this city.
• Мне нра́вятся э́ти фи́льмы. - I like these movies.
• Ей нра́вился го́род, нра́вилась кни́га, нра́вились фи́льмы - the past tense agrees with the thing liked (she liked the city, the book, the movies).
• Ты мне нра́вишься. - I like you.

Нра́виться is not люби́ть: Я люблю́ кино́ - I love movies (in general, always); Мне нра́вится э́тот фильм - I like this movie (a judgment of one particular thing).

examples.en: Let's go to the movies.
Let's sing!
Let's meet at five.

note:
«Let's...» in Russian is дава́й + the «we» form of a perfective verb, or дава́й + the infinitive of an imperfective verb.

• Дава́й пойдём в кино́. - Let's go to the movies.
• Дава́й встре́тимся в пять. - Let's meet at five.
• Дава́й чита́ть. - Let's read.

To several people or politely: дава́йте.

The imperative is formed like this: чита́й, чита́йте; пиши́, пиши́те; иди́, иди́те; -те is added for several people or for the polite «you».

cyr: Verbs with unexpected cases: звони́ть, благодари́ть, поздравля́ть

examples.en: I'll call Mom in the evening.
I thank you for your help.
Happy birthday!

note:
These Russian verbs take cases that English does not lead you to expect:

• звони́ть + dat. - to call someone: Я позвоню́ ма́ме - I'll call Mom.
• благодари́ть + acc. - to thank someone: Благодарю́ вас - I thank you.
• поздравля́ть + acc. + «с» + instr. - to congratulate someone on something: «Поздравля́ю тебя́ с днём рожде́ния» - Happy birthday to you.

Ждать takes the accusative or the genitive: ждать авто́бус, ждать отве́та (to wait for the bus, to wait for an answer).

cyr: Verbs with a preposition: смея́ться над, жени́ться на, ду́мать о

examples.en: They are laughing at you.
He married a Russian woman.
I miss you.

note:
These verbs take a preposition and a case that you cannot guess from English:

• смея́ться над + instr. - to laugh at someone: Они́ смею́тся над ним.
• жени́ться на + prep. - (of a man) to marry someone: Он жени́лся на ней.
• вы́йти за́муж за + acc. - (of a woman) to marry someone
• ду́мать о + prep. - to think of someone: Я ду́маю о тебе́.
• скуча́ть по + dat. - to miss someone: Я скуча́ю по тебе́ - I miss you.

English «to marry» takes a plain object, but Russian жени́ться and вы́йти за́муж always need their preposition.

examples.en: We play soccer on Saturdays.
He plays the guitar.
Do you use this phone?

related.en: to do (a sport, a subject), to study

note:
Four verbs, four constructions:

• игра́ть в + acc. - to play a game or sport: игра́ть в футбо́л, в ша́хматы
• игра́ть на + prep. - to play an instrument: игра́ть на гита́ре, на пиани́но
• по́льзоваться + instr. - to use: по́льзоваться телефо́ном, интерне́том
• занима́ться + instr. - to do, to study: занима́ться спо́ртом, занима́ться ру́сским

In English these verbs take a plain object (play soccer, play the guitar, use a phone); in Russian the preposition or the case is part of the verb.

examples.en: This is a gift for Mom.
Thank you for your help!
I'm going to get some bread.

related.en: for (a reason, a price); (go) to get

note:
English «for» is split into three cases in Russian.

• для + gen. - purpose, benefit: пода́рок для ма́мы (a gift for Mom), ко́мната для госте́й (a room for guests)
• за + acc. - reason, price: спаси́бо за по́мощь (thanks for the help), плати́ть за обе́д (to pay for lunch)
• за + instr. - going to fetch: идти́ за хле́бом (to go get bread), пойти́ за молоко́м (to go get milk)

So «thanks for...» does not use для, and «to go for bread» is за + instr.

examples.en: I speak Russian well.
We talked on the phone.
On Saturdays we go to the swimming pool.

note:
Russian по + dat. has several meanings.

• по телефо́ну, по по́чте - by phone, by mail
• по у́лице, по го́роду - along the street, around the city (moving about)
• по понеде́льникам, по вечера́м - on Mondays, in the evenings (always, regularly)
• по-ру́сски - in Russian: говори́ть по-ру́сски

Remember also: по-ру́сски is written with a hyphen, and «по ру́сски» does not exist.

examples.en: We'll meet in an hour.
He left an hour ago.
I did it in an hour.

note:
English «in an hour» is two different things in Russian, and «ago» is a third:

• че́рез + acc. - in (from now): Я приду́ че́рез час - I'll come in an hour.
• назад - ago: Он ушёл час наза́д - He left an hour ago. Наза́д comes after the time expression.
• за + acc. - within, taking: Я сде́лал э́то за час - I did it in an hour (it took an hour).

The trap is «in an hour»: it can be че́рез час (from now) or за час (finished within that time).

examples.en: We're arriving in May.
The movie starts at seven o'clock.
Today is May 1st.

note:
English «on», «in» and «at» with a day, a month and an hour take different cases in Russian.

• day - в + acc.: в понеде́льник, в пя́тницу, в суббо́ту
• month - в + prep.: в ма́е, в а́вгусте
• hour - в + acc.: в пять часо́в, в два часа́, в час

Date: a neuter ordinal number + the month in the genitive.
• Сего́дня пе́рвое ма́я. - Today is May 1st.
• Когда́? Пе́рвого ма́я. - When? On May 1st.

No в is used with a date.

examples.en: This is a very important problem.
My coffee has gone cold.
I need a coat.

note:
English has no grammatical gender, so these nouns are worth learning one by one: their gender often surprises learners.

• пробле́ма, систе́ма, програ́мма - feminine, because they end in -а: ва́жная пробле́ма
• боль - feminine: си́льная боль (strong pain)
• мето́д - masculine
• ко́фе - masculine, does not change: чёрный ко́фе (black coffee)
• пальто́, кино́, метро́, такси́ - neuter, do not change: моё пальто́ (my coat)

examples.en: Buy some milk and bread.
I don't drink water.

note:
Russian «о» sounds like a clear «о» only in a stressed syllable. In the syllable right before the stress it is read as «а» (as in «father»), and in other unstressed syllables as a very short, weak «а» (as in «sofa»).

• молоко́ - approximately «малако́»
• хорошо́ - «харашо́»
• вода́ - «вада́»

It is always written «о», never «а»: молоко́, not «малоко». So the stress matters: it decides how every «о» in the word is read. This is called «а́канье».

examples.en: My sister lives in Moscow.
What language are you learning?

note:
Unstressed «е» and «я» before the stressed syllable and at the end of a word are pronounced as a short «и» (as in «bit»), not as a clear «ye» or «ya».

• сестра́ - «систра́»
• язы́к - «изы́к»
• де́вять - «де́вить»
• до́ме (в до́ме) - «до́ми»

Under stress «е» and «я» are clear: нет, мя́со, пять. A clear «е» in сестра́ at once gives a foreigner away.

cyr: The letter ы: a sound English does not have

examples.en: I was at home all day.
I bought soap.

note:
«Ы» is a sound between «и» and «у»: say «и» (as in «machine») with the tongue pulled back and the lips not spread into a smile.

• мы - we, вы - you, ты - you (informal)
• быть - to be, бить - to beat
• мы́ло - soap, ми́ло - sweet, cute

The difference in the sound changes the meaning, so you need to hear it.

Spelling rules:
• «ы» is not written at the beginning of a word
• after «г», «к», «х» «и» is written: кни́ги, ру́ки
• after «ж», «ш», «ц» «и» is written, but it is read as «ы»: жизнь, ши́на, цирк

examples.en: We need a little more salt.
My teacher is very kind.

note:
The soft sign «ь» has no sound of its own: it makes the consonant before it soft. «Ль» is like «ly» in «million» and «нь» is like «ny» in «canyon».

• конь - horse
• учи́тель - teacher
• у́голь - coal, but у́гол - corner (no «ь», a hard «л»)

Any other consonant can be soft as well: мать, есть, семь - «т», «с» and «м» are soft, and English has no letter for that.

After «ж», «ш», «ч», «щ» the «ь» does not change the pronunciation, it only shows the feminine gender: ночь, мышь.

examples.en: We live in the first entrance.
This is a family from Serbia.

note:
«Ъ» is rare: it is written only after a prefix ending in a consonant, before the letters «е», «ё», «ю», «я». It means that the consonant stays hard and that a «y» sound (as in «yes») is heard before the vowel.

• объяви́ть - to announce, read «об-йави́ть»
• подъе́зд - entrance of a building, «под-йе́зд»
• съесть - to eat up, «с-йесть»

The soft sign «ь» works similarly before the same letters, but it also softens the consonant: семья́ - «семйа́», статья́ - «статйа́».

cyr: The sound «y» and the letters ч, щ, дж

examples.en: Tea with lemon, please.
He bought jeans.

note:
The English «y» (as in «yes») is written in two ways in Russian:
• й - after a vowel: мой, май, чай
• я, е, ё, ю - at the start of a word or after a vowel: я (I), есть (there is), моё (my, n.), юг (south)

After a consonant these letters do not add a «y» sound: they only soften the consonant before them: нет is like «nyet».

Russian «ч» is like «ch» in «church»: чай. «Щ» is a long, soft «shch», as in «fresh cheese»: борщ. The English «j» as in «jeans» is written «дж»: джи́нсы.

cyr: The letter ё: always stressed, often written as е

examples.en: I understood everything.
Everyone has already gone home.

note:
«Ё» is read as «yo» (as in «yonder») and is always stressed, so it never needs a stress mark.

In books, newspapers and messages the two dots are usually left out and a plain «е» is written. So the stress has to be known:
• все - everyone, всё - everything
• не́бо - sky, нёбо - palate
• лёд - ice, read «lyot»

After a consonant «ё» does not add a «y» sound: it softens the consonant and is read like «о».

examples.en: We looked around the old castle.
The door lock is broken.

note:
Russian stress is free: it can fall on any syllable, it is not shown in normal writing, and it can move between the forms of a word:
• рука́ - ру́ку
• голова́ - го́лову
• го́род - города́ (pl.)

The stress can also change the meaning: за́мок - castle, замо́к - lock; му́ка - torment, мука́ - flour.

A stressed vowel is clear and strong, an unstressed one is weakened (see the notes on «а́канье»). So learn each word with its stress, as the cards show it.

cyr: Voiced consonants at the end of a word

examples.en: Give me the bread.
Let's meet at the station.

note:
At the end of a word a Russian voiced consonant is pronounced voiceless, but it is written as usual.

• хлеб - «хлеп»
• го́род - «го́рат»
• друг - «друк»
• нож - «нош»

The same happens in the middle of a word when a voiced and a voiceless consonant meet: ска́зка - «ска́ска», вокза́л - «вагза́л».

The spelling does not change, only the pronunciation.

cyr: The letter г is read as в in -ого and -его

examples.en: I've known him for a long time.
The weather is nice today.

note:
In the endings «-ого» and «-его» of adjectives and pronouns the letter «г» is read as «в». It is written «г», but you hear «v».

• его́ - «ево́»
• но́вого - «но́вово»
• како́го - «каково́»
• ничего́ - «ничево́»
• сего́дня - «сево́дня»

Words without that ending are an exception: мно́го, до́рого, стро́го are read with «г».

cyr: How to read что, чтобы and конечно

examples.en: Of course, I'll help.
I'm bored without you.

note:
In что and что́бы the letters «чт» are read as «шт»: что - «што», что́бы - «што́бы». Что means «what».

It is the same in a few common words:
• коне́чно - «коне́шно», of course
• ску́чно - «ску́шно», boring
• наро́чно - «наро́шно», on purpose

It is not so everywhere: то́чно and ночно́й are read with «ч».

cyr: Serbian names and places in Russian text

examples.en: We're flying to Belgrade.
She is Serbian, and he is Russian.

note:
Russian writes foreign names by ear, and it has no letters for the Serbian sounds đ, ć, dž and j, so Serbian names look different.

• Đoković - Джо́кович (đ becomes «дж», -ić becomes «-ич»)
• Jovanović - Йо́ванович
• Beograd - Белгра́д
• Srbija - Се́рбия

Every surname in -ić ends in «-ич» in Russian.

The adjective is се́рбский, a Serbian man is серб, a Serbian woman is се́рбка. The Serbian language is се́рбский язы́к.

cyr: Ты and Вы, first name and patronymic

examples.ru: [Вы] не подскажете, как пройти на вокзал?
examples.en: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the station?
What is your patronymic?

related.en: patronymic (a name made from the father's first name)

note:
Russian has two words for «you»: «ты» for close friends, family and children, and «Вы» for strangers, older people and formal situations. «Вы» is also the plural. In a letter or message to one person «Вы» is written with a capital letter.

The switch to «ты» is made by agreement: Дава́йте на «ты».

Russians have an о́тчество, a middle name made from the father's first name. With «Вы» people usually use the first name and the patronymic: Ива́н Петро́вич, Мари́я Ива́новна. The first name alone means a closer relationship.

examples.en: Hello, I'm calling about the ad.
Bye, see you tomorrow!

note:
Greetings depend on «ты» or «Вы»:
• здра́вствуйте - formal, at any time of day (the first «в» is not pronounced)
• приве́т - informal, for both hello and goodbye
• до́брый день, до́брый ве́чер, до́брое у́тро - by the time of day

Goodbyes:
• до свида́ния - formal
• пока́ - informal, like «bye»
• споко́йной но́чи - good night, before going to sleep

Здо́рово! is an informal greeting, but it also means «great».

examples.en: Pass the salt, please.
- Thanks for the help! - You're welcome.

related.en: please; here you are; you're welcome

note:
Пожа́луйста covers several English expressions:
• please - when you ask for something
• here you are - when you hand something over
• you're welcome - as a reply to thanks

Thanks:
• спаси́бо - thank you (from «спаси Бог»)
• благодарю́ - I thank you, formal or in writing

Another reply to thanks: не́ за что - don't mention it.

When you did not hear something and ask «pardon?», you do not say пожа́луйста, but что? or прости́те?

examples.en: - How's the movie? - Not bad, it's watchable.
- Sorry, I'm late. - Never mind.

note:
In conversation ничего́ is often not «nothing» but a mild answer:
• Как дела́? - Ничего́. = Not bad, so-so.
• Извини́те! - Ничего́. = It's all right, never mind.
• Ничего́ стра́шного. = No harm done.
• Ничего́ себе́! = Wow! Look at that! (surprise)

Норма́льно is similar: Как дела́? - Норма́льно. = Fine, OK.

examples.en: Let's meet at seven.
- Okay, I'm off. - Alright, bye!

note:
Дава́й(те) most often means «let's»:
• Дава́й встре́тимся! - Let's meet.
• Ла́дно, дава́й. - Okay, talk to you later (at the end of a conversation).
• Дава́йте - for «Вы» or several people.

It is followed by the «we» form of a perfective verb: дава́й пойдём, дава́й позвони́м.

Дава́й is also the imperative of дава́ть, «to give»: Дава́й де́ньги! - Give me the money! The meaning is clear from the sentence.

examples.en: Let's go home, it's already late.
Everyone got into the car. - Off we go!

note:
«Let's go» in Russian is пошли́ (on foot) and пое́хали (by vehicle).
• Пошли́ в кино́! - Let's go to the movies.
• Пое́хали! - Off we go! (by car or train; also when something is starting)

Пошли́ is also the imperative of посла́ть (to send) and the past plural of пойти́, so only the context tells them apart.

Пошли́ ему письмо́ - Send him a letter.
Они пошли́ домо́й - They went home.

examples.en: Wait a minute.
Pour me a little water.

note:
In conversation Russian often uses diminutives, and not only about children:
